claims.text: The premelting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by the interplay between surface energy and grain-boundary energy.
The melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by the interplay between surface energy and grain-boundary energy.
The balance of surface and grain-boundary energies dictates the stability of the nanoparticles' crystalline structure against thermal fluctuations.
Grain-boundary and surface morphology mediate the thermal behavior of the nanoparticles.
Thermally activated atomic diffusion contributes to premelting and melting behavior.
Thermally activated grain-boundary migration contributes to premelting and melting behavior.
Premelting temperature scales with nanoparticle size.
Melting temperature scales with nanoparticle size.
Premelting temperature varies systematically with alloy composition.
Melting temperature varies systematically with alloy composition.
The predicted size- and composition-dependent temperatures reflect the balance between surface and grain-boundary energies.
Quantum effects may dominate for particle sizes below 10 nm.
Vaporization may occur at temperatures above 1000 K.
A vacuum or inert atmosphere prevents oxidation or contamination during heating.
There is a lack of direct experimental evidence for the specific role of grain-boundary energy in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
